# RustyNES v2.9.4 — "Plumb"

The first release of the line to v3.0.0, and a quiet one by design: **no emulation behaviour changes**. It records what v3.0.0 now is, brings the project's records back in line with its code, and makes CI run tests it had only been linting.

## v3.0.0, decided

[ADR 0043](https://github.com/doublegate/RustyNES/blob/main/docs/adr/0043-v3-is-the-api-major-and-a-release-candidate-core.md) makes **v3.0.0 the API major with a release-candidate core**:

- ADR 0042's removals, the `LockstepBus` rename and the save-state bus-section bump;
- both MiSTer bitstreams, labelled **not hardware-verified**.

Hardware verification — the SuperStation One board session and the mobile device runs — becomes a later v3.x. The path there is [`to-dos/plans/v2.9.4-to-v3.0.0-line-plan.md`](https://github.com/doublegate/RustyNES/blob/main/to-dos/plans/v2.9.4-to-v3.0.0-line-plan.md):

| Release | Subject |
| --- | --- |
| v2.9.4 | records and CI (this one) |
| v2.9.5 | accuracy |
| v2.9.6 | mappers |
| v2.9.7 | targeted platform features |
| v2.9.8 | performance and the SDRAM arbiter |
| v2.9.9 | the release candidate |

## CI now runs what it only linted

- **Tests behind non-default features:**
  - frontend with `full`: 659 lib tests, against 618 by default and 631 with `av-record`;
  - `rustynes-core` and `rustynes-ppu` with `debug-hooks,hd-pack`: +13 and +5;
  - `rustynes-apu` with `debug-hooks`: +10;
  - `rustynes-script` with `script-ipc,script-sqlite`: +7.

  All of these tests existed and passed; no job had ever run them.
- **The eight fuzz targets** are built and run in CI, 20,000 inputs each from a fixed seed. Before this, no workflow even compiled them. A panic planted in one target failed the job.
- **Line coverage**, which was never measured before, is now **72.01%** over the workspace's lib tests. CI fails below 70%. The integration suites are out of scope, because instrumented they are too slow for a per-change job.
- **A weekly toolchain canary** on stable and beta shows the cost of moving the 1.96 pin while it is small. It never blocks a merge.
- **`rustynes-cheevos`** now meets the workspace lint set for the first time; 92 warnings are fixed.

## Records, re-checked against the code

- **`docs/STATUS.md` mapper tiers:** 174 families, 51 Core / 95 Curated / 28 BestEffort. It said 172 and 26.
- **Test counts, store status, roadmap tables:** corrected. In particular, no app-store launch has happened; Android ships as GitHub sideload and iOS through TestFlight.
- **The deferred-features catalogue:** last reconciled at v2.3.9. 25 of its open entries turned out to have shipped, and each is now ticked with the file that proves it.
- **The OAM-decay model is recorded as derived from Mesen2.** It was added at v2.1.4 by a commit that said so, but the provenance records never listed it. `ppu.rs`'s header, `NOTICE` and `docs/originality-and-provenance.md` now do. The code is unchanged; both projects are GPL-3.0-or-later.
- **Found, and planned for v2.9.7:** the Settings "Overclock (extra scanlines)" field saves a value that nothing reads.

## The MiSTer core

The RTL is unchanged; the only `rtl/` edit is a comment. So the bitstreams attached here are **v2.9.2's files, byte for byte**, as for v2.9.3:

- on-die md5 `c17b0f37d5c49b150c023734b583f468`;
- off-die md5 `75ae3a99e840e29675ded9898dae127d`.

Two other changes on the MiSTer side:

- **Every skip in the co-simulation ladder is now counted.** Seven per-cycle bus gates skipped when their golden was missing without reaching the TOTAL line. A new audit keeps it that way.
- **The records were corrected:** gate counts, the off-die status, the battery-save comment that said "not implemented", the contribution checklist, and the board kit re-staged against the released pair.

**No hardware has run any bitstream.**

## Install

- Download the pre-built binaries for Linux, macOS, and Windows below.
- The MiSTer core bitstreams are attached below: `RustyNES_MiSTer-v2.9.4.rbf` (on-die, also as `RustyNES_20260928.rbf`) and `RustyNES_MiSTer-v2.9.4-offdie.rbf`. They are v2.9.2's files, so the MiSTer menu shows build date 260928. Neither has run on hardware.
- The WebAssembly build is live at [doublegate.github.io/RustyNES](https://doublegate.github.io/RustyNES/).
- The RetroArch core is in RetroArch's Online Updater on the platforms the libretro buildbot publishes to.
